text:
ella: quick thought — what if we add a short-lived "reservoir reservation" window to handle sub-10s spikes without stealing from the long-tail fairness pool?
priya: hmm, window as in reserve X tokens per tenant for Y seconds and then reconcile? sounds like backfilled credits.
sam: love the idea for UX for bursty tenants, but worry about oscillation if probes + reserve windows interact. remember last time with probe-induced spikes? :grimacing: 
ella: exactly, we need a reconciliation step that applies a strict decay and a probe-dampener so probes can't trigger repeated reservations. sketch: reserve_limit=1000, window=12s, reconcile_decay=0.25
ops-bot: deploy-bot: note — previous experiment (A/B) showed 7% tail-latency increase when reservation leaked into shared pool.
james: can we make the reserve ephemeral and charged to an isolation bucket? like a soft-lease: if not used, it returns; if used, it's billed and deducted from next period. that limits abuse.
priya: charge-on-use is good. tradeoffs: makes billing slightly delayed and increases accounting complexity. instrumentation must surface "reserved but unused" metrics.
sam: operationally, we need to avoid creating a new single point of truth. prefer implementing reservation at admission proxy (stateless) using sliding-window counters and letting central allocator reconcile asynchronously.
ella: yeah — admission proxy could hand out short signed tokens for reserve amount. token contains tenant-id, amount, expiry, nonce. central reconciler verifies and debits if redeemed. sample token payload:
```
{ "tenant": "tenant-123", "amount": 150, "exp": 1719800012, "nonce": "abc123" }
```
priya: signing flow is fine, but we must ensure clock skew safety and idempotency. what about replay? nonce + central store lookup adds cost.
james: store lookups are okay if we batch them. central reconciler can accept batched redeems and apply a deterministic ordering by nonce; use a small in-memory LRU to mitigate replays at the proxy.
sam: still worried about fairness: VIP tenants could monopolize reservation slots repeatedly. propose a weighted cooldown: if tenant redeems reservation more than N times in M minutes, their reservation weight halves for the next window.
ella: that gives a soft backpressure signal without hard eviction. we should prototype the weighted-cooldown policy in the simulator before an infra change.
priya: agree. can someone add a short sim (10k tenants, poisson spikes, probe actors) and measure tail latency, fairness index (Jain), and cost delta? I can help with metrics and dashboards.
james: I'll take the sim. quick checklist:
- sim config and synthetic probes (sam)
- reconcile sign/token flow sketch (ella)
- metrics to capture: reserved_unused_count, reservation_redeem_rate, cooldown_triggers (priya)
- rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool for 48h, auto rollback on >3% tail-latency or fairness index drop >0.05 (ops)
sam: add a kill-switch flag at the proxy to disable reservation without redeploy. super useful for incidents. :+1:
ops-bot: checklist created: https://rwd.internal/checklists/reservoir-reserve-window
ella: thanks. james — ping me when the sim PR is up and we can run the first baseline. I'll draft a short RFC addendum describing token format and reconciliation contract.
priya: and I'll add telemetry dashboards and an alert runbook for cooldown storms.
james: will do. filing PR after standup.
ella: cool, closing the loop: goal is to reduce 95th pt spikes from short probes without harming long-term fairness. keep it small and observable. :seedling:
